transcript: He got down onto the edge of the grip and sat with his boots in the ash. Say it, said Torrin, later. Say it now. I want it now. Rook looked out at the pasture, where there was a mule and a cart on its side, and four hundred pounds of gray lying about in a road, and then down into a ditch at a boy with a broken arm and his leg opened, and both hands full of a thing nobody had a word for. It isn't called anything, he said. Then he put two fingers on the inside of Torrin's wrist, the way he had done on a towpath in the spring and at the road cut before that, and held them there for three seconds, and...
